title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel / disconnect / reconnect + server timeouts (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Clarkson
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent streaming sessions left in limbo when clients closed connections unexpectedly, or when transient network issues caused disconnects. This caused wasted GPU cycles in the serving runtime and inconsistent behavior across the OpenAI compatibility layer (some clients expect resumable streams, others expect a hard cancel). This PR standardizes lifecycle controls for streaming: explicit client-cancel semantics, graceful server-side handling of TCP disconnects, a reconnect/resume token protocol, and server timeout safeguards to prevent runaway work.  Summary of changes: - Add explicit client-cancel control (HTTP/WS message type and OpenAI-compat header handling) so clients can signal intent to abort generation and free KV caches immediately. - Improve disconnect handling: server now marks streams as disconnected and transitions model worker to a cancellable state; background KV cache remains available for short resume windows. - Implement reconnect/resume token flow: server issues a short-lived resume token in-stream metadata; reconnects with the token attempt to resume the previous session's KV cache and offsets. Fallback to soft-restart if token expired or incompatible. - Server-side timeouts: two configurable timeouts (inactivity_timeout and max_run_timeout) to ensure resources are reclaimed. Inactivity timeout triggers earlier when no active network ack from client. max_run_timeout enforces absolute upper bound on generation. Both are surfaced via API and OpenAI compatibility headers. - OpenAI compatibility: add header mappings and behavior toggles so existing OpenAI-compat clients see expected responses (499-style semantics for client-cancel, resume behavior aligned with documented token life). - Tests: add unit + integration tests for cancel, disconnect/reconnect flows and timeout edge cases. - Docs: update streaming lifecycle and compat docs with examples and recommended client behavior.  Behavior notes: - Client-cancel: clients POST a cancel frame (or send application/json {"action":"cancel"} on WS). Server responds with a final partial stream with a metadata footer {"redwood": {"status":"cancelled","code":499}} and immediately frees execution state. This mirrors many client expectations while keeping observability hooks. - Disconnect vs cancel: a TCP/WS disconnect is treated as 'disconnected' not immediately cancelled; server keeps short-lived resume state (default 45s inactivity_timeout) to allow reconnection. If reconnect not received within inactivity_timeout, session is implicitly cancelled and resources reclaimed. - Reconnect/resume tokens: resume token issued as base64 encoded JSON in-stream metadata (short-lived, opaque to clients). Reconnect attempts are validated for model/version/seq-compat; incompatible attempts fallback to a clean start with a clear final metadata indicating resume failure. - Server timeouts: max_run_timeout defaults to 5 minutes for safety but is configurable per route. On timeout the server emits an error footer {"redwood": {"status":"timeout","code":504}} and attempts a best-effort flush of partial tokens to the client.  Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_lifecycle_controls. Initial rollout to Dedicated and Hosted Canary region, measure cancellation reclaim rates and 95th percentile extra GPU hold-time.  Related: ENG-1423 (streaming reclaim), ENG-2187 (openai-compat resume), SUP-901 (customer incident: stuck streaming sessions).

squash: streaming lifecycle controls: client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, server timeouts (OpenAI compat)

See ENG-1423, ENG-2187 for context.
release_notes: Add explicit client-cancel message to streaming API; server frees resources on cancel (status=cancelled, code=499)
Support reconnect/resume via short-lived resume tokens for transient disconnects (default resume window: 45s)
Introduce inactivity_timeout and max_run_timeout to guard long-running streams (defaults: 45s inactivity, 300s max run)
OpenAI compatibility: header mappings and behavior to match common client expectations; documented in docs/openai-compat/streaming.md
